subject.title: [Feature Request]: one-line local bootstrap for daemon + dashboard auth + Telegram owner setup

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class one-line local bootstrap contract for daemon, dashboard auth, and Telegram owner allowlist/preapproval, or keep these as separate setup steps?
rationale: The remaining gap is not a narrow bug: it changes setup UX, channel auth defaults, and the Telegram owner trust boundary, and repository policy treats these as compatibility and security-sensitive surfaces.

options.title: Approve narrow core bootstrap
options.body: Add or extend non-interactive onboarding/bootstrap so it composes gateway setup, dashboard URL delivery, Telegram token setup, and Telegram-owned numeric owner allowlist/preapproval with explicit risk acknowledgement.

options.title: Keep manual composition
options.body: Document the supported sequence using existing onboard, dashboard, channels add, channels resolve, config set, and pairing commands, and close or narrow this feature request.

options.title: Split into narrower issues
options.body: Track Telegram owner default/allowlist changes in the related Telegram issues first, then revisit a one-line bootstrap wrapper after the security model is settled.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow core bootstrap
recommendation.body: Add or extend non-interactive onboarding/bootstrap so it composes gateway setup, dashboard URL delivery, Telegram token setup, and Telegram-owned numeric owner allowlist/preapproval with explicit risk acknowledgement.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest history across setup, Telegram setup wizard, and channel capability boundaries touched by this product choice.
